item.title: See you next time, Shenzhen!
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
A city of innovation, a vibrant cityscape and warm hospitality. Shenzhen has given visitors from around the world plenty of reasons to fall in love with the city. As APEC China 2026 drew to a close, some international guests were already looking forward to coming back. Until next time, Shenzhen!

item.title: Peng champions cultural bonds, mutual learning
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
China is willing to enhance cultural exchanges and mutual learning with the rest of the world, Peng Liyuan, wife of President Xi Jinping, said on Thursday while experiencing a cultural showcase with the spouses of leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation economies in Shenzhen, Guangdong province. Peng warmly greeted the guests at the Shenzhen Bay Culture Square, and they watched festive and vibrant Xingshi and Yingge dance performances presented by a group of children. Xingshi, which literally means awakening the lion, is a southern-style lion dance, while Yingge is an artful fusion of dance, drama and martial arts that has long been popular in Guangdong's Chaoshan region, comprising the cities of Shantou, Chaozhou and Jieyang. Both dances are listed as China's national intangible cultural heritage. Peng and the guests also toured an exhibition showcasing efforts to preserve and pass on local intangible cultural heritage. They viewed with interest exquisite handicraft items, enjoyed an artistic performance featuring Lingnan culture, and experienced a digital presentation of local arcade streets. Lingnan culture — an important part of Chinese culture — embodies the wisdom of harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature, Peng told the guests, adding that China is willing to enhance cultural exchanges and mutual learning with the rest of the world. The guests spoke highly of the long history and richness of traditional Chinese culture and the achievements made in advancing Chinese modernization. They also expressed their willingness to enhance exchanges and cooperation with China. At the end of their visit, Peng and the guests, who included the wives of the leaders of Chile, Vietnam, the Republic of Korea and the Philippines, posed for a group photo. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi meets Thai PM in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping on Friday called for promoting the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to a higher level. China and Thailand should continuously enhance political mutual trust and strengthen solidarity and coordination, Xi said when meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province. The two countries should step up exchanges between governments, political parties, legislatures and at other levels, and safeguard their common strategic interests, Xi stressed. He called on the two sides to make good use of cooperation mechanisms in economy and trade, science and technology, and the digital economy, expand and strengthen traditional cooperation in agriculture and connectivity, and cultivate and strengthen new growth areas of cooperation such as artificial intelligence, new energy vehicles, aviation and aerospace, disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, and water resources management. The two sides should strengthen cooperation in culture, education, and tourism, Xi added. He also urged intensifying efforts to crack down on illegal and criminal activities such as online gambling and telecom fraud. The two sides should strengthen multilateral coordination and work together to safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi said. China is ready to play a positive role in bringing about an early turnaround in Thailand-Cambodia relations, Xi said. For his part, Anutin said Thailand is ready to continue to strengthen high-level exchanges with China and enhance cooperation in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, industrial and supply chains, and connectivity. Thailand will resolutely crack down on cross-border crimes including online gambling and telecom fraud, and protect the safety of Chinese citizens in Thailand, he said, adding that the country welcomes more Chinese visitors. Anutin attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, held from Wednesday to Thursday.

item.title: Xi says China ready for closer cooperation with Malaysia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN -- China stands ready to foster greater momentum for cooperation with Malaysia to bring more benefits to people of both countries, President Xi Jinping said Friday. China-Malaysia relations have maintained high-level development since the two sides reached important consensus on building a high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future and ushered in a new "Golden 50 Years" for bilateral ties in April last year, he said. Xi made the remarks when meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province. China and Malaysia should maintain high-level strategic communication and support each other in safeguarding their respective national sovereignty, security and development interests, Xi said at the meeting. The two sides should also ensure high-quality development and operation of key projects, expand and improve agricultural product trade, and broaden cooperation in tourism, education and other areas, he added. Xi called for joint efforts to advance the reform of global governance, strengthen coordination and cooperation within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, and safeguard the common interests of developing countries. Anwar said the Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and Malaysia firmly adheres to the One-China principle. He said Malaysia is ready to strengthen strategic coordination with China, give full play to the role of bilateral cooperation mechanisms, ensure the sound operation of key infrastructure projects, and enhance cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence. Malaysia will also promote inter-civilization exchanges and dialogue, step up coordination and collaboration in international affairs, and keep elevating the level of Malaysia-China relations, Anwar said. Anwar attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen.

item.title: China, Russia and US commit to safeguarding global peace, stability
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
The leaders of China, Russia and the United States stressed their shared commitment to maintaining strategic stability and international security at a historic trilateral summit on Thursday, pledging to advance United Nations reform, increase energy supplies and hold talks on reducing nuclear risks. President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump made the commitment in the China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, issued following their unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province. "The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought," the declaration said, adding that the three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. As permanent members of the UN Security Council, the three countries will remain committed to reforming the UN so that it can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security. On energy security, the three countries announced plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, while reaffirming the importance of maintaining stable global energy supplies. The declaration also addressed the jurisdiction of international judicial institutions. The three leaders agreed that the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction. Xi, while presiding over the summit, described the first-ever gathering of the three countries' top leaders as "groundbreaking". He said history has shown that peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos in the world. He stressed that humanity, living in the same global village, is "a community with a shared future where we all stand to benefit or lose together". In this global village, major countries shoulder special responsibilities, with their positive interaction being "not optional, but a must", he said. Xi called on the three countries to set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make a greater contribution to the progress of humanity. The Chinese president made a four-point proposal on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace — staying committed to mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. On mutual respect, he highlighted the need for the three countries to respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, social systems and development paths of their own choice, and their respective core interests and major concerns. On peaceful coexistence, Xi said China, Russia and the US should be partners and friends and avoid conflict or confrontation. The Thucydides Trap is by no means a destiny, he added. Turning to economic cooperation, Xi highlighted the complementary strengths of the three economies and urged them to expand trade and economic ties rather than pursue decoupling or disruptions to supply chains. On dialogue and consultation, he urged joint efforts from the three countries to maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms, to ensure that "misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate". The international community expects major countries to do more to promote peace talks, Xi pointed out, while stressing that China, Russia and the US should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means. Wrapping up the gathering, Xi described the summit as "positive, constructive and fruitful", saying the three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace. As long as dialogue continues and the door to engagement remains open, there is hope for peace, Xi said, while expressing confidence that the seeds planted at the Shenzhen summit would take root and bear fruit. Putin emphasized the importance of sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs and finding mutually acceptable solutions through dialogue and cooperation. Russia stands ready to work with China and the US on the basis of mutual respect and equality, peacefully manage differences, promote free and open international trade, and strengthen cooperation on energy and food security and global governance of artificial intelligence, he said. Trump told the two leaders that the three nuclear powers bear an important responsibility for maintaining global peace and stability, stressing the need to prevent nuclear proliferation and avoid the catastrophic consequences of nuclear weapons. The joint declaration from the China-Russia-US summit indicated that the unprecedented gathering has been successful and has yielded significant outcomes, said Wu Xinbo, dean of the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University. Wu said the four-point proposal put forward by Xi is crucial not only to shaping a new type of major-country relations, but also to guiding relations among countries more broadly in a changing international landscape. He rejected comparisons between the Shenzhen summit and the 1945 Yalta Conference, arguing that the two gatherings differed fundamentally in their purposes. The Yalta Conference was primarily concerned with the postwar division of spheres of influence among major powers, whereas the Shenzhen summit sought to strengthen cooperation among the three countries to promote global peace, security, stability, development and governance, he said. Zhu Feng, dean of the School of International Studies at Nanjing University, said the summit and its declaration reflected a new approach to addressing the challenges of the times. The declaration's central message was that major countries share responsibility for safeguarding world peace, without which sustainable development cannot be achieved, Zhu said. He described the summit as a major breakthrough in head-of-state diplomacy, saying it had helped the three countries establish a greater degree of common understanding about their responsibilities in managing international affairs. xuwei@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi says China, Singapore should strengthen strategic communication, enhance coordination
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Singapore should strengthen strategic communication and enhance solidarity and coordination as the world is undergoing accelerated changes unseen in a century. The two countries should be sincere friends who trust each other and support each other in pursuing development paths suited to their respective national conditions, said Xi when meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province. Wong attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen. During the meeting, Xi called for advancing the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership between China and Singapore to new heights, and stressed the need for both sides to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. The two countries should launch negotiations for upgraded Version 4.0 of their free trade agreement, and deliver signature cooperation outcomes in areas such as the digital economy, green development, and artificial intelligence, Xi added. Noting that both countries should be "a progressive force" for championing international fairness and justice, Xi called for safeguarding regional peace and stability while jointly building an Asia-Pacific community and a community with a shared future for humanity. For his part, Wong stated that Singapore firmly adheres to the One-China principle and opposes "Taiwan independence." Singapore stands ready to work with China to enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in areas such as trade, industrial and supply chains, and artificial intelligence, and promote people-to-people exchanges, the prime minister noted. Wong said Singapore is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the Chinese side on international affairs to jointly address global challenges.

item.title: Xi meets Indonesian president in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Friday announced the launch of negotiations for a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership. The announcement was made during Xi's meeting with Prabowo in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. Xi said the two countries should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust, and jointly guard against and respond to external risks. He called on both countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and clean energy. Xi called for efforts to reach an all-round, high-standard comprehensive economic partnership agreement at an early date. Amid emerging risks and challenges in the world, China is ready to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Indonesia within multilateral frameworks, including the United Nations, APEC and China-ASEAN cooperation, Xi said. Prabowo said Indonesia's strategic partnership with China is stronger than ever, reaffirming that Indonesia firmly adheres to the One-China principle and that Taiwan is a province of the People's Republic of China. Indonesia sincerely welcomes Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in the country, and is committed to providing a reliable, stable and predictable business environment, Prabowo said. Prabowo said Indonesia highly appreciates China's role as a responsible major country in international affairs, and stands ready to work with China to safeguard the shared interests of the Global South and promote regional and global peace and stability.

item.title: Xi says China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping said Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help each other succeed, as the two countries have no historical grievances or conflicts of fundamental interests. China-Australia relations are stable at present, said Xi when meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province. Albanese is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. As next year marks the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Australia, Xi called on the two sides to achieve greater progress in bilateral relations from a new starting point. Xi said that in a volatile and turbulent world, the two countries should enhance mutual trust, accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, and keep to the right direction of friendship and cooperation. He called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in agriculture, energy and minerals, and expanding cooperation in emerging areas such as the green economy, new energy, the digital industry, artificial intelligence and climate change response. Efforts should be made to promote friendship between the two countries through expanded people-to-people exchanges, Xi said, noting that the two sides had agreed to designate 2027 as the China-Australia Year of Tourism. He also emphasized the need to strengthen multilateral coordination in addressing global challenges, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community, and jointly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law. Albanese said that the improvement and development of Australia-China relations serves the interests of both sides and brings tangible benefits to the peoples of both countries. He said that Australia stands ready to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen practical cooperation in trade, investment, AI and other areas, deepen people-to-people exchanges, respect each other and properly handle differences, so as to make Australia-China relations an example for countries with different systems to develop constructive relations.

item.title: Xi: Head-of-state diplomacy 'irreplaceable' for China-US ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
President Xi Jinping highlighted on Thursday the "irreplaceable" role of head-of-state diplomacy in guiding relations between China and the United States, urging concrete actions to sustain the current momentum of stable and positive growth in the relationship. Xi made the remarks during his meeting with US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting. Both sides considered the meeting to be positive and constructive, according to a statement released after the meeting. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive relationship of strategic stability, implement the consensus reached by the two presidents, and build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity, the statement said. This was the third meeting between Xi and Trump this year. The two presidents also met in Beijing in May, when Trump made a state visit to China, and in Washington in September, when Xi made a state visit to the US. Xi said that over the past few months, he and Trump have been working together to explore the right path for China and the US, the two major countries, to get along well with each other. The new vision of building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity has been well recognized by the peoples of both countries and welcomed by the international community, he said. Xi noted that the overall stability and positive momentum of China-US relations have brought tangible benefits to the people of the two countries, and injected stability and certainty into the world. He expressed his hope to continue working with Trump to jointly steer the giant ship of China-US relations in the right direction toward the future. Xi emphasized that building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented, groundbreaking endeavor that requires an enterprising spirit, hard and solid efforts, and the ability to get things done. To sustain the current momentum of stable and positive growth in China-US relations, the key is to take concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state, he said, adding that communication between the working teams on both sides also needs to keep pace. Xi stressed that it is important to make a longer list of cooperation and a shorter list of problems. Differences that cannot be resolved for the time being should be managed in a constructive way to prevent them from escalating, he said. On the Taiwan question, Xi said the US should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-US relations. He called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns and work toward mutual benefit. Cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. He also underlined the need for China and the US to strengthen communication and coordination to guard against security risks of artificial intelligence and ensure that AI always remains under human control. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of US-China relations, adding that both leaders have maintained close contact, with their friendship growing stronger. Trade and investment ties between the two countries have continued to grow, and cooperation on fentanyl and other issues has yielded results, Trump noted. Both sides should maintain the momentum of steady development of bilateral relations, and strengthen cooperation in areas such as farm products, energy and super intelligence, and fairly address each other's concerns, Trump said. He told Xi that the US does not support "Taiwan independence". Trump congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability. The two presidents also discussed regional and international issues of mutual interest. He Yadong, spokesman for the Chinese Ministry of Commerce, announced on Thursday that the agricultural working group under the China-US Board of Trade will soon hold its first meeting. The two countries' economic and trade teams have maintained communication at various levels, and the two sides held the first meeting of the Board of Trade under the China-US economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Nov 13, the spokesman said at a regular news briefing in Beijing. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi calls for inclusive regional co-op based on solidarity, openness, innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
President Xi Jinping outlined economy and trade, connectivity, innovation and development as four pillars for building an Asia-Pacific community and opening up new prospects for regional cooperation, as he chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Thursday. The gathering marked the third time that China has hosted the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting, following those held in Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. "Today, momentous changes not seen in a century are accelerating across the globe," Xi told the leaders and representatives of APEC economies and heads of international organizations attending the meeting. APEC's 21 member economies are home to more than one-third of the world's population and account for over 60 percent of global GDP. Xi called for efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship, he noted, adding that "to navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other". "We must expand our shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily build a shared sense of community," he said. He called for upholding openness and integration, advancing economic integration and championing free and open trade and investment. Development should benefit everyone, he said, while taking into account the different needs of Asia-Pacific economies. Xi said that China, an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, is ready to work with all parties to strengthen the pillar of economy and trade, upgrade the pillar of connectivity, foster the pillar of innovation and enhance the pillar of development. On trade, Xi said the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific is a shared vision of APEC members, and he called for steady progress in realizing this vision and setting a higher standard for openness. He urged efforts to align regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, reduce barriers to trade and investment, and help economies build the capacity to participate in high-standard economic and trade arrangements. Regarding connectivity, he called for stronger infrastructure networks, closer coordination of policies and regulations, and easier travel for business and tourism. Cultural and people-to-people exchanges should also be promoted to foster mutual understanding, he said. On innovation, Xi described the digital economy and artificial intelligence as engines of innovation-driven growth. "We should build an open ecosystem for innovation, encourage the broad application of AI, and promote the innovation-driven transformation and upgrading of industries," he said. On development, he emphasized the need to promote regional cooperation on energy and food security, deepen anti-corruption governance across borders, and expand green and low-carbon cooperation to achieve sustainable economic growth. He also called for improving livelihoods and investing in people to tap into the full potential of talent across the Asia-Pacific. "China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation," Xi said. He announced that China will provide $20 million to support APEC's practical cooperation, and will establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges. China will also set up cooperation institutions in areas including digital technology, cross-border data flows, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, he said. Leaders and representatives of member economies delivered remarks in turn. All parties spoke highly of the fruitful outcomes of the APEC China Year, thanked China for its excellent work, and made positive responses to the major initiatives and measures put forward by Xi. Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund, who was invited to brief the meeting on the state of the global economy, said that AI has had a material impact on global growth this year, helping counterbalance the economic effects of an energy supply shock. Describing AI as a significant factor in medium-term competitiveness, productivity and growth, she called on economies to develop digital infrastructure, prepare workers for the technology, and address risks to financial stability and cybersecurity. She also underscored the importance of dialogue and cooperation through forums such as APEC, saying that working together can help advance shared prosperity and peace. After listening to the other participants' remarks, Xi called for turning the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into action, maintaining a clear direction for cooperation and delivering solid results to continuously achieve tangible and accessible outcomes. At the conclusion of the meeting, leaders adopted the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which puts forward the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, as well as three outcome documents covering trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnamese President To Lam, whose country will host APEC in 2027, welcomed leaders and representatives to attend next year's meeting. With China's leadership and the positive contributions of its members, APEC 2026 has achieved important accomplishments, adding momentum to economic integration and development in the Asia-Pacific, he said. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn
